## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing before merge: the parser drops `--wait` completely, while the ADR added in this pull request says `--wait` stays as an alias for one release and warns when used. Existing scripts that pass `--wait` will exit with an argparse error. This review read all of `app/cli.py`, `tests/test_cli.py` and the new ADR, and searched the repository for other uses of `wait` and `timeout`; `app/cli.py` is the only consumer of the renamed attribute. One verified strength: the default (30) and the `json`/`csv` format choices are unchanged, as the PR body says, and the tests check both.

## Changes
The pull request renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout` in `parse_args` and updates the tests to match. It also adds ADR 007, which describes the terminology change, and a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Keep `--wait` as a deprecated alias for `--timeout` — `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now fails with "unrecognized arguments" and exit code 2, because the only option defined is `--timeout`. The ADR added in this diff says "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." (docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5), but the code has no alias and no warning, and no test passes `--wait`. — Any existing script or automation that calls the CLI with `--wait` stops working right after this release, with no deprecation period, which contradicts the decision this pull request records. — Fix: Register `--wait` with `dest="timeout"` and a custom `argparse.Action` that calls `warnings.warn(..., DeprecationWarning)` (or writes to stderr) before storing the value. Then add tests checking that `["--wait", "12"]` gives `args.timeout == 12` and emits the warning, and that `--timeout` does not warn.
